summary: Re-review of all 16 units. All seven round-1 fixes were verified: reliability 0.05/0.0025 = 20 (twenty-fold) with a correct bathtub description; guard distance S = K(t_response + t_stop) + C is stated consistently, keys 0.40 m (worked example) and 0.82 m (Q008: 1.6 x 0.45 + 0.10) are right and each stem states its inputs; the substitution example is now a genuine substitution; the DFA redesign count 14 - 3 + 1 - 4 + 2 = 10 with N_min = 6, 49 s gives E = 18/49 = 0.367 and a 61% time saving; the review-conduct major-action wording now matches the lesson definition; the Action Priority sentence is hedged. Every numeric key and worked example was recomputed in Python (torsion, shaft diameter, safety factor, break-even, DFA, RPN, series/parallel/exponential reliability, stacks, RSS, fits, float, TAR, uncertainty, budgets, margins) and all agree with the keys and tolerances. A scan of the parsed text found no control or tab characters, python format placeholders, e+06-style numbers, plain x in LaTeX, placeholder steps or stale option-letter references. Only two minor points remain. This is an AI review: standards values (ISO 13855 K and C, AIAG-VDA Action Priority) were recalled and not checked against the documents, and the course still needs a subject-matter expert before engineering reliance.

issues.problem: In both decision-matrix worked examples (scoring and sensitivity) the three per-concept steps all begin with the identical text "Weighted total for this concept: multiply each score by its weight and add." without naming the concept; only the LaTeX (S_A, S_B, S_C) says which concept is computed. Read as plain text the steps are indistinguishable.
issues.suggestedFix: Name the concept in each step, for example "Concept A: multiply each score by its weight and add."

issues.problem: The lesson says ISO 13855 uses 2000 mm/s for distances up to 500 mm, yet the worked example (K = 1.6 m/s) yields 0.40 m, inside that range, and the question of acceptability at 0.30 m is also below 500 mm. The example is flagged as assumed, but a student may take 0.40 m as a standard-compliant answer (the standard's K would give about 0.50 m). Standards detail unverified here; source check recommended.
issues.suggestedFix: Add a half-sentence to the worked example, for example "With K = 2.0 m/s as ISO 13855 specifies for distances up to 500 mm, the result would be 0.50 m; K = 1.6 m/s is used here only to practise the formula."
